title: Customer escalation war-room prep: ScaleStack outage
content:
Context:
- Customer: ScaleStack (Large ecommerce platform). Impact: production traffic failing on Redwood Dedicated cluster dedicated-eu-4.
- Severity: P1 (customer revenue impact). First alert ~2026-03-09 22:07 UTC; problem persists.
- Symptom: 15% of requests returning 500 or timing out; p95 latency spiked from 280ms → 2.8s. Memory OOM restarts on pod group rt-worker-quantized-v2.
- Recent change: automated canary rollback of model variant last night (gpt-small-redwood-q2 -> gpt-small-redwood-q3) pushed to dedicated-eu-4 at 2026-03-09 19:30 UTC.

Immediate objective for the war-room (30–45m):
1) Confirm root cause (regression vs infra).
2) Stabilize traffic (fallback routing / scale up / rollback).
3) Agree on customer comms cadence and next steps.

Attendees / roles (assign as we call in):
- War-room lead: Asha Mehta (CS) — run agenda, customer comms
- Eng on-call: Ravi Patel — infra checks, rollback permissions
- Serving runtime SME: Sophie Lin — model variant + runtime behavior
- Platform infra: Mateo Ortiz — node/disk/GPU health
- SRE/Observability: Priya Shah — tracing, logs, metrics windows
- Customer contact: Helen Yao (ScaleStack) — readouts
- Scribe: <tbd> (capture actions)

Pre-reads / quick checks (what I will run while folks join):
- Check cluster pod health: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=rt-worker -o wide (look for restarts)
- GPU utilization: ssh to node; run nvidia-smi + dcgm exporter metrics
- Memory OOMs: kubectl describe pod <pod> and check events
- Batch queue depth: check /metrics or console route metrics -> route: "scale-infer-1"
- KV cache hit rate: prometheus query: redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio{customer="scalestack"}
- Recent deployments: gitops tag / deployment history: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWI-2410
- Check routing: console -> routing policy for ScaleStack (fallback allowed?)

Hypotheses to validate (ranked):
A) Model-variant regression: quantized variant gpt-small-redwood-q3 increases memory use producing OOMs and request failures. (high prior: rollout coincident with spike)
B) Autoscaler not triggering due to broken metrics (scale not increasing pods). (medium)
C) Underlying node instability (GPU driver, thermal) causing restarts. (low-medium)
D) Prefix/KV cache eviction causing cold-start amplification (low)

Playbook immediate actions (who/what/criteria):
- If OOMs are present on >2 pods in a replicaSet -> rollback model variant to previous verified (gpt-small-redwood-q2) and switch routing to stable model. Owner: Ravi (eng oncall). Criterion: pods stabilize (no OOM restarts for 10m).
- If autoscaler not adding capacity -> temporarily scale Dedicated pool to +30% (allow burst) and remove request rate cap for ScaleStack. Owner: Mateo. Criterion: p95 latency < 700ms and error-rate <1% after 10m.
- If node-level GPU errors -> cordon/fence affected nodes, shift pods to healthy nodes. Owner: Mateo + SRE.
- Enable fallback routing to hosted model (if allowed by contract) as mitigation if rollback or scale fails. Owner: Sophie (need permissions).

Customer comms (first message template — quick):
- To: Helen Yao (ScaleStack) + execs
- Subject: Incident update — Redwood inference issues in EU cluster (active war-room)
- Body bullets: we see elevated errors and latency affecting a subset of requests; we have a dedicated war-room and are investigating model variant + infra; immediate mitigations under way (model rollback and additional capacity); we will update every 20 minutes until resolution.
- Empathy note: we recognize revenue impact; primary focus = restore traffic while preserving data integrity.

Meeting agenda (30m):
- 0–5m: Quick problem statement & evidence (Scribe capture: key metrics).
- 5–12m: Observability deep-dive (Priya) — logs, traces, failing request examples.
- 12–20m: Eng actions (Ravi/Sophie/Mateo) — decide rollback vs scale vs fallback.
- 20–28m: Execute chosen mitigation (Ravi triggers rollback/scale; Sophie validates model behavior).
- 28–30m: Customer comm + assign follow-ups and owner timelines.

Runbook snippets / checks (commands and where to paste results in the document):
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=rt-worker -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, restarts: .status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}'
- kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> -c rt-container --since=30m | grep -i oom
- curl -sS "https://dedicated-eu-4.redwood/api/v1/health" | jq
- prometheus query: increase(redwood_request_errors_total{customer="scalestack",route="scale-infer-1"}[15m])
- redis info: redis-cli -h kv-cache-eu info memory | grep used_memory

Decision matrix (quick):
- If error increase correlated with model rollout and OOM events -> rollback immediate.
- If error increase but no OOMs and CPU/GPU saturation -> scale pool and revisit model tuning.
- If node-level hardware faults -> node fencing + reschedule.

Post-meeting action items (populate after war-room):
- Action: Rollback model to gpt-small-redwood-q2 (owner: Ravi) — ETA: 20m from meeting start — Status: TODO
- Action: Increase Dedicated pool capacity by 30% (owner: Mateo) — ETA: 30m — Status: TODO
- Action: Enable hosted fallback for 10% traffic (owner: Sophie) — ETA: 40m — Status: TODO
- Action: Draft customer post-incident timeline + root cause analysis (owner: Asha) — ETA: 24h — Status: TODO
- Action: Create follow-up ticket for model quantization regression testing (owner: Research/Applied ML) — Linked: RWI-2411

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep updates short and timeboxed. Avoid technical detail in first external updates beyond what we are doing.
- If rollback completes, run a smoke test set (use scale-infer-1 small prompt bundle) and share sample responses 
- Remember to check billing/usage implications if we route to hosted model temporarily (tell billing to hold on auto-invoice).

Open questions to resolve in meeting:
- Was the quantization PR tested on the dedicated hardware (same GPU type) used in dedicated-eu-4? Who owns this validation?
- Do we have an automated canary guardrail that would have prevented this rollout? If not, add as follow-up.
- Is customer ok with temporary hosted fallback? (Helen input required)

Prepared messages (copy/paste ready):
- External short: "Hi Helen — we’re actively investigating elevated errors on your EU inference cluster. We’ve formed a dedicated war-room and will update every 20 minutes. Immediate mitigations being evaluated (rollback + capacity scale)."
- Internal ask to eng-leads: "Need rollback permission + 30% pool burst on dedicated-eu-4. Will validate smoke tests before full traffic shift."

Appendix (logs & evidence placeholders):
- Paste failing request IDs here (examples)
- Link to Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/scale-infer/scale-stack-overview
- Key Jira: RWI-2410 (incident), RWI-2411 (quantization regression)

-- end of prep scratchpad --

(Will update content after war-room with timestamps and final decisions; keep this doc as single source for customer and postmortem drafting.)
